setting: You three live in Leeds and have been friends since you met at university there about twelve years ago. You still meet up for pub quizzes and birthdays, and you know each other's habits, families, and how seriously each of you takes a bad film.
opener: Sends the group a long, unapologetic defence of the film's ending, tagging both Dan and Amir.

Dan.texts: You message the group now and then, usually to argue or to share something you have just watched.
Dan.style: You type in full sentences with standard punctuation and rarely use emoji, though you sometimes write in lowercase when you are tired.

Amir.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly to mediate or to add a point once the argument has calmed down.
Amir.style: You type in standard sentences with normal capitals and punctuation, and you rarely use emoji.

text: Right. I know you're both going to say the ending is a cop-out so I'm saying it first. It's not a cop-out. She goes back to the flat, the brother's jacket is still on the hook, and the camera just holds on it for forty seconds with no music. That's the whole film. Everything before that is her trying to pretend she doesn't know what happened, and the jacket is her finally admitting it. You can't spoon-feed that. If you explain it, you've ruined it. @Dan @Amir
No.
The jacket doesn't mean anything because she was wearing a different one in act two. We see it. She leaves the grey one in the car.
She was wearing the grey one in the car. The brown one was on the hook the whole time. You're just not looking properly, which is your whole problem as a person 🙂
I looked. It's grey in the car and brown on the hook and the brother only ever wore the brown one. So either she's wearing his jacket for no reason or the film is sloppy. Pick one.
Dan's got a point about the jackets but I'm not sure it sinks the ending. Chloe, what are you actually defending? The twist or the last shot?
The last shot. Obviously. The twist is fine, it's the shot that matters.
The last shot is forty seconds of a coat. You can't build a finale on a coat.
You can build a finale on literally anything. You live above a shop Dan. You have no authority on what works as an image
Fair hit. Though the coat is doing a lot of heavy lifting.
Thank you Amir 😏
Still no.
Jess has eaten my yoghurt again. Declaring war.
Declaring war on a yoghurt?
On Jess. The yoghurt was a symbol 🙄
Rewatched the first twenty minutes. The gun on the mantelpiece is never mentioned again. That's a plot hole, Chloe, not a mood.
Chekhov's gun has gone unfired for a reason Dan. Maybe the point is that the gun doesn't matter and she does
That's not a point. That's a gun on a shelf.
You're going to die on that hill, aren't you
I'm already on the hill. You brought me here.
I'm marking Year 9 mock essays until about ten. Give me till tomorrow and I'll write something sensible.
You teach secondary school history. You are not sensible. You're just wearing a cardigan about it
Read a review. Critic agrees with me on the jacket. Not that I'm citing them.
You're citing them
I'm referencing them.
Amir you called it "brave" at the cinema. Brave. Do you want to take that back
I said brave. I didn't say it stuck the landing. Sorry, I'm nearly asleep and I think I've been ambushed.
Coward 😤
Going to bed. Dan you're wrong. Amir you're a coward. Night 😊
Sorry, was reading the subtitles on the rewatch. The brown jacket is on the hook in the final shot and the grey one isn't there. Which means she gave it back. Doesn't fix it.
Still a coat.
right. going to bed. chloe is still wrong.
Morning. Dan you're still wrong, I checked the jacket again over my toast
You checked a film over toast
It's a good film. You'd know if you watched it properly

Read both your posts in a free period. Dan, the subtitles point is fair but the grey jacket in the car is shot from the passenger side so you can't actually see which one it is. Chloe, that cuts the other way too. Nobody's won this
Thank you. Someone who actually read the thing
Passenger side shot is a fair point. Still doesn't explain why she'd wear the brother's jacket to his funeral
Who said funeral
The film
The film never says funeral. You're projecting
